summary: Round 6 frontend-only verification of the two SwipeDeck fixes (stacking order via variant zIndex + removal of dragConstraints/elastic with custom onDragEnd). All targeted behaviours pass on desktop 1440x900 against the external preview URL. No code changes were made.
critical_code_review_comments: SwipeDeck.tsx cleanly implements both fixes (variants carry zIndex, mode='sync', dragSnapToOrigin=false, animate() fallback for sub-threshold drags). No further issues observed in that file.

Minor nit (not blocking): the previous-direction enter variant uses opacity 0.9 — fine, but worth noting the incoming card is briefly ~90% opaque while on top of the outgoing one; visually acceptable.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Deck geometry unchanged (bbox ~271x240 in right column at ~x=1125,y=372 on 1440x900). Items array has 5 WatchItems and advances show1→film1→show2→film2→show3→wrap. zIndex sampling via getComputedStyle(card).zIndex works; mid-transition there are exactly 2 deck-card elements for ~300ms. The exiting card's title can be used to disambiguate exiting vs entering across samples. Fresh page reload resets the hint and wiggle one-shot.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs reproduced. Both prescribed fixes work as described: (a) framer-motion applies variant zIndex as an inline style — exiting card renders at z=3 and entering at z=1 for next (dir=1), and inverted (enter z=3, exit z=1) for previous (dir=-1); pile peek divs are z-0. (b) With dragConstraints/elastic removed and dragSnapToOrigin={false}, a committed swipe's x value increases monotonically from the released position toward ±480 with no back-flicker; sub-threshold drags spring back via animate(x,0,...) without changing the index.
